design:
Tier 2: outward-facing. Pushing a branch and opening a PR publishes the work on GitHub, and cannot be taken back once seen. Hence: off by default, refused without a GitHub remote and a logged-in GitHub CLI, and the acceptance drive's merge step is the operator's.

Migration: adds columns only (a project's PR landing and squash settings; a build's PR number, URL, state and when it was last checked). Rollback: the columns are unused by the main and nowhere landings, so downgrading drops them with no effect on existing builds.

Flow:
CURRENT   task approved -> landing checks on merged tree -> Hub merges into main
PROPOSED  task approved -> landing checks on build branch + task -> pushed
            first task: draft PR opened against main
            all tasks approved: PR marked ready; a send-back: back to draft
          something starts from main / operator looks -> Hub asks GitHub
            merged -> tasks landed -> local main fast-forwarded if safe, else 'behind GitHub' + Update
            closed -> tasks not landed, branch kept

The landing queue's merge to main is replaced for these builds by a push to the build branch; checking still goes through the queue, so the two-concurrent-check limit and the known-failing list apply unchanged.

open_questions.question: Which branch does the PR target? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): the project's main branch, master here, merged only on GitHub under the repository's own PR rules.
When does the Hub ask GitHub? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): on actions, not a timer (FR asks-on-actions).
Local main after a merge? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): fast-forward when safe, else show 'behind GitHub' with Update (FR local-main).
Checks before a push? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): the landing-phase checks locally until slice 2.
Main moving while the PR is open? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): the Hub merges it into the build branch; a conflict goes to the builder.
The drive's merged case? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): one human step, merging a PR that changes only testbed/README.md.

problem:
A build has two landings today: merged into main by the Hub, or nowhere (hub/hub/builds.py:47-49; the Build dialog's route accepts only those two, hub/hub/api/v1/spec.py:568). Nothing in the Hub talks to a code host. A team that lands work through pull requests, with CI and a person's review on the host, cannot use AgentWeave's builds without giving that up or carrying the work across by hand.

Decisions made by the operator on 2026-11-04 (roadmap design) and 2026-11-06 (this document): one PR per build; the agents' own review still happens first; squash or not is a project setting; the user's own GitHub CLI login is used; draft at the first approved task, ready when all are approved, back to draft on a send-back; never on by default; the PR targets the project's main branch and is merged only on GitHub, under that repository's own PR rules; the Hub asks GitHub on actions, not on a timer; it brings the local main forward only when that is safe; landing-phase checks still run locally until slice 2; main moving on GitHub is merged into the build branch by the Hub.

requirements.rationale: Pushing publishes the work; it must be a choice, never a default.
requirements.statement: A project has PR landing off until the operator turns it on in the project's settings; a build's landing can be 'pull request' only in a project that has it on, and a Build request naming it in any other project is refused with a reason that names the setting.

requirements.rationale: Found at the start, not at the first approved task after hours of work.
requirements.statement: Turning PR landing on, and starting a build whose landing is 'pull request', are refused with a reason naming the problem when the project directory has no GitHub remote, when the GitHub CLI is not installed, or when it is not logged in.

requirements.rationale: Until slice 2 the PR's CI is not the gate, so the PR must only ever hold work that passed the full local check.
requirements.statement: An approved task of a PR build is pushed only after the project's landing-phase checks pass on the build branch with the task merged in, judged against the known-failing list as any landing is; a failing task is sent back as a landing failure is today and nothing is pushed for it.

When the first task of a PR build has passed its checks, the Hub pushes the build branch to the project's GitHub remote and opens a draft PR from it against the project's main branch; each later task that passes is pushed to the same branch, and the build keeps one PR.

The PR is marked ready for review once every task of the build has been pushed, and is returned to draft when any task of the build is sent back while the PR is open, until every task has been pushed again.

The PR's title is the spec's title, and its description names the spec document, each requirement the build serves by identifier and statement, the accepted evidence for each requirement, and each task with its state; the description is rewritten on every push and every draft or ready change.

requirements.rationale: Replacing a branch someone else pushed to would destroy their work.
requirements.statement: A project with PR landing on chooses whether the build branch carries one commit per task as built or a single commit holding the whole build; with the single commit, each push replaces the branch's commit only if the branch on GitHub is still the one the Hub last pushed, and otherwise the push is refused and shown on the build.

Before each push, when the project's main branch on GitHub holds commits the build branch does not, the Hub merges GitHub's main into the build branch; a conflict sends the task being pushed back to its builder, as a merge conflict on landing does today, and nothing is pushed.

requirements.rationale: The state matters only when something is about to start from main or the operator is looking (operator, 2026-11-06). A slow GitHub must not freeze turn starts.
requirements.statement: While a build's PR is open, the Hub asks GitHub for its state when a build starts in that project, when a task branch or worktree is created in it, before each push to the PR, when the operator opens the build or the project, when the Hub starts, and when the operator presses 'check now' on the build; it does not ask on a schedule, and asking never delays a turn starting.

A PR found merged on GitHub records every task of its build as landed, naming the merge commit; a PR found closed without merging records them as not landed, and the build branch is kept on GitHub and locally.

requirements.rationale: The next build must start from the merged work, and the Hub never touches a checkout holding the operator's changes.
requirements.statement: After a PR is found merged, the Hub fetches from GitHub and moves the project's local main to GitHub's main only when that is a fast-forward and the main branch is not checked out with uncommitted changes; otherwise it shows on the project that main is behind GitHub, with an Update button that does the same fast-forward once it is safe and says why when it is not.

requirements.rationale: Teams that land through PRs keep their own rules (operator, 2026-11-06).
requirements.statement: The Hub never merges the PR, changes its base branch, approves it, or changes the repository's branch protection or required reviews and checks; the only GitHub operations it issues are pushing the build branch and opening, editing, drafting, readying and reading its PR.

The build card and each of its tasks show the PR's link and state (draft, ready, merged, closed) and when the Hub last asked GitHub; a failed push or a failed ask is shown on the build with GitHub's error.

in_scope: A third build landing, pull request, available only in a project that has turned PR landing on
Pushing a build branch and opening, updating, drafting and readying its PR against the project's main branch, through the user's GitHub CLI login
The PR's description: spec, requirements, accepted evidence, task list
Asking GitHub for an open PR's state on actions, and recording the build's work as landed or not landed
Bringing the project's local main up to date after a merge when that is safe
Showing the PR's link and state on the build and its tasks
non_goals: Merging the PR, or bypassing the host's PR rules: merging happens only on GitHub
Waiting for the PR's CI as the full check (slice 2)
Review comments on the PR coming back as send-backs (slice 3)
Switching this repository's normal builds to PR landing
Per-project tokens or a GitHub App
Webhooks: a local app cannot receive them
A timer that asks GitHub on a schedule (operator, 2026-11-06; reconsider in slices 2 and 3, which wait on CI and on reviewers)

summary: A build whose landing is "pull request" puts its approved work on one GitHub pull request against the project's main branch, instead of merging into main itself. The PR opens as a draft at the first approved task, gains each later approved task, is marked ready when every task is approved, and returns to draft when a task is sent back. Its description carries the spec, requirements and accepted evidence. The PR is merged only on GitHub, under that repository's own rules. The Hub asks GitHub for the PR's state when something is about to start from main or the operator looks (no timer), records the work as landed or not, and brings the local main up to date when that is safe. Product, opt-in per project. This repository stays on direct merges for its normal builds.
